modelResponse.episodeSummary: 70yo male, Third-degree AV block with wide QRS escape, critical severity, hemodynamically unstable (MAP 59).
modelResponse.rhythm: Third-degree (complete) heart block with wide QRS escape rhythm
keyECGEvidence: morphology: AV dissociation; wide QRS escape; tall peaked symmetric T waves; flattened P waves
preEventNote: Progressive PR prolongation then AV dissociation; QRS widening over 20 min
modelResponse.mechanism: Excess extracellular potassium depolarizes the resting membrane potential of myocardial cells, reducing the availability of sodium channels and impairing conduction through the AV node and ventricular myocardium, leading to progressive conduction delay and eventual complete AV dissociation.
contributingFactors: End-stage renal disease with missed last 2 dialysis sessions
Use of potassium-sparing medications (Lisinopril 20 mg, Spironolactone 25 mg)
Metabolic acidosis (pH 7.24 LOW, bicarbonate 15 mmol/L LOW)

rejectedAlternatives.why: While bradycardia can occur in inferior MI, the presence of 'tall peaked symmetric T waves', 'flattened P waves', and a history of missed dialysis with K 7.4 mmol/L strongly points to metabolic etiology over ischemic.
No such medications listed in home medications; the progressive QRS widening and peaked T waves are pathognomonic for hyperkalemia.

recommendedActions: Calcium gluconate or calcium chloride IV immediately to stabilize myocardial membrane
Urgent hemodialysis (indicated by missed sessions and K 7.4 mmol/L)
Insulin (10 units IV) with Dextrose to shift potassium intracellularly
Consider Albuterol nebulization to further lower serum potassium
